Together with the thresholds, these selections keep the radiative propagator denominators away from zero and suppress the collinear enhancement of vacuum radiation and its associated angular sensitivity [17, 20]. This selection also aims to reduce dilution of the enhancement signal by spontaneous emission outside the background field. Far from the nuclei, the enhancement factor approaches unity, so such contributions would reduce the occupation number inferred from R−1. Residual outside-field contributions should therefore be assessed as a source of systematic dilution. Quantifying this effect requires an analysis of the space-time overlap between the radiation formation region and the background field.
